result.title: SpecForge: Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents via Behavioral Specifications
result.summary: Coding agents based on frozen language models can improve their performance by refining the external context they rely on, without updating model weights. We study recursive self-improvement through behavioral specifications: natural-language code documentation that describes the behavior of program entities and guides agents in generating correct code. We formulate a self-improvement loop in which an agent generates code from its current specifications, evaluates it with execution-verified tests, and refines the specifications based on observed failures. The improved specifications then guide subsequent generation, progressively improving the agent's understanding of the codebase. However, recursive refinement is challenging because program entities are interdependent. Improving the specification of one entity can inadvertently degrade the correctness of others, a phenomenon we call output coupling. This creates a whack-a-mole effect in which local improvements cause regressions elsewhere, preventing consistent progress. We introduce SpecForge, a multi-frontier tree search framework that addresses this challenge with three mechanisms: (i) Pareto-guided state selection preserves complementary specification states and prevents premature commitment; (ii) dependency-constrained entity selection prioritizes callee-before-caller refinement; and (iii) error-diversified expansion explores multiple refinements using different subsets of test failures. On DevEval+, SpecForge achieves the best performance across five backbone models, including a 94.9% solve rate with Claude-4.5-Sonnet and a 5.7-percentage-point average improvement over the strongest baseline. The improved specifications also make the agent better at tasks outside the loop: they transfer to cross-language translation and to new-feature implementation, where they outperform the benchmark-provided requirement documents.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SpecForge，把自然语言「行为规范」当作可迭代改进的外部状态：agent 依规范生成代码、用执行验证的测试评估、再依失败结果重写规范，并以多前沿树搜索缓解实体相互依赖带来的「打地鼠」式回退，在 DevEval+ 上提升多款骨干模型的解题率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「生成—执行验证—改写中间状态」的递归循环、Pareto 状态保留与按失败子集多样化扩展，可能为 latent 推理轨迹的搜索、互补状态保留与停机/收敛判据提供可供核查的线索；但本文针对代码 agent 的外部文本规范，不涉及视觉或多模态内部状态。
